:::note[About this page]
This page is generated from the `tools/list` response of [s1000d-writer-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/writer-mcp/) 0.8.0. The s1000d-writer-mcp page explains the configuration and how to read the responses.
:::

## Summary

Changes the structure of an existing procedural or descriptive data module: inserts, removes or moves a node. Places are `location.path` values, and a node to insert is a draft node (`step`, `para`, `admonition`, `listItem`). Only the edited ranges of the original text are rewritten; every other character stays as it was. Without `marking`, it changes neither the issue information nor change markup (`changeType` and so on). With `marking`, it adds change markup to an in-work issue. A result with XSD errors that the edits introduced is not written

## Description returned by `tools/list`

This is the text an LLM receives.

> Change the structure of an EXISTING procedural or descriptive data module: insert a node, remove a node, move a node. Places are location.path values of the document as it is now (s1000d-reader-mcp read_data_module returns them); with several edits, every place still refers to the document before any edit. A node to insert is a structured draft node (step / para / admonition / listItem), never XML. All edits are applied or none: refusals[] gives the reason per edit (for example id-referenced, not-allowed-here, unsupported-node, released-issue). Only the edited ranges of the original text are rewritten; the rest stays character for character, and a moved element keeps its content unchanged. Elements that can be removed or moved: proceduralStep, para, warning, caution, note, listItem. Without "marking" this tool does NOT change the issue information or add change markup (changeType, changeMark, reasonForUpdate): a released issue (inWork "00") is refused unless allowReleasedIssue is true. With "marking" it adds change markup on an IN-WORK issue (start one with start_revision): an inserted node gets changeType="add"; a removed node is KEPT and gets changeType="delete" (changes[].kept); a move is accepted only within the same parent, which gets changeType="modify"; edits inside an element already marked add or delete get no markup; reasonForUpdate tells which reason the markup refers to. The result is verified again; XSD errors that the edits introduced come back in newSchemaErrors[] and such a result is never written. Returns applied, xml (unless includeXml is false), changes[] (each with mark when change markup was added), reasonForUpdate (with marking), refusals[], newSchemaErrors[], referencedFromOtherObjects[], verification, fixes[] (without candidates for the new XSD errors: change the edits and call again instead). Writes only when write is true (a path is overwritten in place).

## Arguments

The content of `inputSchema`. A nested argument is written as `parent.child`, and an item of an array as `parent[].child`.

| Name | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` |  |  | File path of the document. |
| `xml` | `string` |  |  | An existing document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB). Not for XML you wrote yourself: build new data modules with build_data_module. |
| `csdbDirs` | `array<string>` |  |  | CSDB folders used to resolve references, find BREX and number new objects (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). The FIRST folder is also where write: true writes (it may not exist yet). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); other folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes. |
| `edits` | `array<object>` | Yes | items ≥ 1 |  |
| `edits[].op` | `string` | Yes | `insert` / `remove` / `move` |  |
| `edits[].at` | `string` |  |  | remove / move: location.path of the node to remove or move. |
| `edits[].to` | `string` |  |  | insert / move: location.path of the reference node (the node beside or inside which the node goes). |
| `edits[].position` | `string` |  | `before` / `after` / `first-child` / `last-child` | insert / move: before / after the reference node, or as the first / last child of it. | `marking` | `object` |  |  | Add change markup for these edits (in-work issue only; issueType must be changed, status, rinstate-changed or rinstate-status). Give exactly ONE of reason and reasonRefId: "reason" adds a new reasonForUpdate and the markup refers to it (first edit for that reason; urt01 is refused, an editorial change has no change markup); "reasonRefId" is the id of a reasonForUpdate ALREADY in the status element (later edits for the same reason; nothing is added). One call = one reason: call again for edits with another reason. Omit marking to edit without change markup. |
| `marking.reason` | `object` |  |  | One reason for update (reasonForUpdate in the status element). The text and the type are the user's: never fill them in. |
| `marking.reason.text` | `string` | Yes | length ≥ 1 | The text of the reason (one simplePara). |
| `marking.reason.updateReasonType` | `string` | Yes | pattern `^urt[0-9]{2}$` | S1000D updateReasonType, written as given: urt01 editorial change (no change markup may refer to it), urt02 technical change, urt03 markup only, urt04 applicability only, urt05 references only; urt51-urt99 are project values. Required: it is never chosen for you. |
| `marking.reason.updateHighlight` | `string` |  | `0` / `1` | "1": this reason goes into the Highlights data module. |
| `marking.reason.id` | `string` |  |  | reasonForUpdate/@id. Omit it: an id that is not in the document is made (rfu-0001 …). An id already in the document is refused. |
| `marking.reasonRefId` | `string` |  |  | id of a reasonForUpdate already in the document (identAndStatus.reasonForUpdates[].id from s1000d-reader-mcp, or reasonForUpdate.id of an earlier response). |
| `marking.changeMark` | `string` | Yes | `0` / `1` | "1": show a change mark (change bar) for these changes; "0": do not. The project decides; ask the user. |
| `allowReleasedIssue` | `boolean` |  |  | Edit a released issue (issueInfo/@inWork "00") in place, without changing the issue information or adding change markup. Default false. Set it only when the user has said so: the result does not follow the S1000D rules for updating a released data module. It has no effect with marking (a released issue is then always refused). |
| `product` | `object` |  |  | The product to evaluate applicability for. attributes: ACT productAttribute id → value; conditions: CCT cond id → value. Omit to skip the applicability check. |
| `product.attributes` | `object` |  |  |  |
| `product.conditions` | `object` |  |  |  |
| `write` | `boolean` |  | default `false` | Write the result into the CSDB (the first folder of csdbDirs / S1000D_CSDB_DIR). Default false: the XML is only returned. Nothing is written when the XML is not valid against the XSD unless allowInvalid is true. |
| `overwrite` | `boolean` |  | default `false` | With write: true, replace a file of the same name. Default false: an existing file is left alone and reported as write-conflict. |
| `allowInvalid` | `boolean` |  |  | Write even though the document was ALREADY invalid against the XSD before the edits. It does not allow writing a result with new XSD errors. |
| `includeXml` | `boolean` |  |  | Include the XML in the response (default: true when write is false, false when write is true). Pass false to keep the response small when you only need changes[], refusals[], newSchemaErrors[] and verification. |
| `maxFixes` | `integer` |  | default `50`, ≥ 1, ≤ 1000 | Cap on the remaining fixes listed in the response (default 50). |
